abstract:
We prove a power improvement for uniform Collatz interval compression. Let $C$ be the shortcut Collatz map, let $J_h$ count odd steps, put $\theta=H_2(\log_3 2)$, and set $k=\lceil\log_2m\rceil$. For fixed $\gamma>0$ and $K<\infty$, every interval of $m$ consecutive nonnegative integers produces at most $Km^{\theta-\gamma}$ distinct pairs $(C^{k^2}(x),J_{k^2}(x))$. The first version's effective logarithmic improvement and its proof are retained; the new power threshold is ineffective.

The arithmetic input transports signed numerator relations through actual residue carries using a fixed-place Subspace argument. Triangular parity coding and a balanced entropy recursion give dimensions approaching one at fixed Rényi orders on suitable positive linear precision bands. Independent groups amplify the exceptional-environment exponent to give full min-entropy bounds. These hold separately at every exact total in a prescribed asymptotically critical window.

An exact duality extends the argument to the joint source and endpoint law. At total precision $P=p+h\log_2 3$, the raw pair modulo $(3^h,2^p)$ has maximum atom at most $C_d2^{-dP}$ for every $d<1$ on a sufficiently small positive linear band. One shared canonical carry costs a factor $s$. The resulting averaged source-guessing bound remains valid when the endpoint residue and total clock are revealed. Bands may shrink with the target dimension.

Real interval estimates for the normalized source and endpoint also yield a power saving for large final odd-step counts, without an earlier-count restriction. The original-source count bounds halving failures among any $m$ consecutive positive integers by $Km^{\theta-\gamma}$ at clock $k+\lfloor k/8\rfloor$. Distinct-state orbit zeta sums converge below $\theta$. Fixed exact checks support the algebraic interfaces; asymptotic claims rest on proofs. No full uniformity, atom lower bound, or individual descent guarantee is claimed. Collatz remains unresolved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Adds Theorem A: G_(k^2)(m)<=K*m^(theta-gamma) for fixed gamma>0, uniformly in original interval location and with endpoint/count labels and common clock. The effective Theorem1 and its proof are preserved. Adds complete Section7 TheoremB: fixed-order signed numerator relations, actual residue transport by a coefficient-uniform two-dimensional Subspace lemma, balanced entropy triangle recursion giving D_r increasing to1 on bands with upper slope rho/2^r, bounded-coarse-alphabet concentration at one fixed Renyi order, and every asymptotically critical exact total by a comparison law centered at that total. Section8 gives the full original-source Holder-Chernoff and finite-clock compression deduction, plus orbit-set sparsity and zeta convergence at some exponents belowtheta. New constants/thresholds are ineffective; no full binary uniformity or universal descent is claimed. Adds one frozen five-case finite audit of the new coding/factorization inputs and its author audits; all original supplement code, results and figure/data are unchanged and were not rerun. Incorporates the prior reviewer-requested comparison with Mahler paper27/v1 Section6 and precise preceding discussion links. Credits Rees, Leen, accepted paper30/v2, Bilu/Schlickewei, Tao and bounded differences; title/abstract now lead with the power improvement. Adds TheoremC in Section7.9: for every d<1, full raw min-entropy at least d*p-O(1) on some positive linear band depending on d, including every asymptotically critical exact total; canonical loss is log2s. Local-good events depend only on each group's coarse totals. Young's inequality combines enough good actual conditional laws, and independence before conditioning amplifies the bad-environment exponent. A separate clock tail bound enforces uniform arithmetic ranges. This implies all finite Renyi orders, including collision entropy, but no uniform atom lower bound or unit dimension on a fixed positive linear band. Complete proof and author audit included; no further experiment. Adds Section8.2: among any m consecutive positive integers, at most K*m^(theta-gamma) fail to halve within k+floor(k/8) shortcut steps, k=ceil(log2m). Also bounds exceptions at each input's own dyadic clock up to X. Complete original-source deduction from S37, uniform high-part bounds, the origin block by dyadic subdivision, and ordinary-clock translation included. No optimality claim or new experiment. Adds TheoremD in Section7.10: joint source/endpoint concentration at total precision P=p+rho*h, using exact raw duality, one shared canonical carry, central chunk placement and a two-prime separation product. Gives fixed Renyi and full atom bounds on suitable bands, every critical exact total, and averaged conditional source guessing with endpoint and total revealed. Canonicalization occurs before environment mixing. Compares Mahler36/v1. Includes the full argument, author audit, and one fixed exact raw-duality check (1103 words,36193 chunks); previous experiments remain frozen. No pointwise conditional bound, bounded normalized energy or lower occupancy is asserted. Adds TheoremE Section7.11: real interval concentration for both normalized raw source and endpoint, optionally retaining source residues modulo3^h. A near-output Subspace lemma and explicit quantization/carry bounds extend the conditional entropy and full-atom proof. Section8.3 gives the exact source-fraction consumer: uniformly in intervals of width2^k, the count with J_T>=alpha*T-H is at most C_H*k*2^(theta*k-(d-theta)*floor(delta*k)), T=k+floor(delta*k), for suitable fixed d>theta and small delta>0. It needs no earlier-count or survival condition; halving follows as a corollary. Complete proof and author audit, no new experiment. Records the all-one-atom limit on broader unconditioned real precision; no arbitrary-small-power survival or universal descent is asserted.
title: A power improvement for uniform Collatz interval compression
